title: Business Analyst Roadmap
summary: Build technical literacy alongside requirements analysis, SQL, process modelling, stakeholder communication, Agile delivery and business-domain knowledge.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030. The semester milestones can be shifted to match the university calendar.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Requirements analysis, SQL, process modelling, Agile, documentation, presentation, stakeholder work and internship experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Product/business analysis, technology consulting, data/BI analysis, enterprise applications or a specific industry domain.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead analysis, solution definition, business cases, product decisions, process transformation and cross-functional delivery.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Enterprise transformation, strategic analysis, AI-enabled business processes, architecture and executive-level technology advisory.

rows.text: Programming basics, Git, spreadsheets and structured problem solving

Process map + 20 user stories + acceptance criteria + prioritized backlog
Data analysis, dashboards, root-cause analysis and business cases
Dashboard + 2-page insight report + quantified business recommendation
Internship/project case study showing problem → analysis → solution → outcome
Solution evaluation, APIs, enterprise systems and project economics
Solution options matrix + API/process map + cost/benefit analysis
3 polished BA case studies + 5 mock case interviews + targeted resume

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If you take the four-year honours/research variant, use the additional year for a substantial business-transformation project, research, advanced analytics, enterprise systems, AI-enabled process analysis or an industry capstone.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move from documenting requirements to shaping business problems, evaluating alternatives and measuring outcomes. Build knowledge in one industry—such as banking, healthcare, telecom, retail or manufacturing—and learn how AI changes business processes without losing the ability to validate requirements with real users.

PhD routes

Move from gathering and documenting requirements toward owning business problems and transformation outcomes. Maintain enough technical knowledge to evaluate systems, data and AI proposals while developing deeper expertise in an industry and in organisational strategy.
